subject: Insurance
title: The Law of Large Numbers
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Law of Large Numbers usable.

hook.text: Flip a coin 10 times and you might get 7 heads. Flip it 10,000 times and you'll get almost exactly 50%.

buildup.text: Insurance works the same way. One person's fate is unpredictable.

discovery.text: An insurer can't predict if you will die this year.

twist.text: The law breaks down with correlated risks.

climax.text: The law of large numbers is insurance's mathematical engine. Pool enough risk and randomness becomes predictable.

punchline.text: One person: unpredictable. One million: almost certain.

quiz.question: Why does the law of large numbers matter for insurance?
options: It makes aggregate risk predictable across large pools
